title: O God! Who Knowest How Frail We Are
description: O God! Who Knowest How Frail We Are in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: William Gaskell wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 34, “Seeking Strength”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O God! who knowest how frail we are, How soon the thought of good de-parts; We pray that Thou wouldst feed the fount Of ho-ly yearn-ing in our hearts.

lines: O God! who knowest how frail we are,
How soon the thought of good departs;
We pray that Thou wouldst feed the fount
Of holy yearning in our hearts.
Let not the choking cares of earth
The precious springs of life o'ergrow;
But, ever guarded by Thy love,
Still purer may their waters flow.
To Thee, with sweeter hope and trust,
Be every day our spirits given;
And may we, while we walk on earth,
Walk more as citizens of heaven.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Gaskell died in 1884.
credits: Words by William Gaskell (1805–1884), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
